utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, is everybody on? Sven, I can hear typing, are you muted?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Not muted, it's just the keyboard. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: No worries. Quick one first, did anyone read Samir's email about the printer contract?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: The renewal? I skimmed it on the train.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is that the one with the three-year term?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: That's the one. Three years, and nobody here asked for three years.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: It's about eleven percent over what we pay now. I checked the PDF twice.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Eleven percent for the same four machines. Great.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'll push back on it, that one's mine. Okay, so the real item. Second step for staff sign-in. Passwords by themselves are-

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Not enough, no. The audit pretty much said so.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, Clara put it in the findings and-

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Did she say what kind of second step, though?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: No, she left that open. She just wants something in place by, um, end of next month, roughly.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: So end of April. That's a bit under seven weeks from today.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ish, yeah. So I'd like to get close to a pick today, because I don't want this sliding into next quarter.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Are we looking at the whole range? Apps, keys, all of it?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Nobody's brought a list, honestly. Wei, you were poking at this last week, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Um, a little, yeah. I think maybe the easiest thing is, you know, a code goes to their phone by text each time they sign in, and they type it in.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Text messages. Seriously?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I mean, it's just, uh, it's one option, I'm not saying it's perfect-

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, go on, I'm only asking. People always say those can be intercepted.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Let him finish, Mateo. Wei?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right, so, nobody has to buy anything. There's about 220 of us and everyone already carries a phone.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: And I think maybe we could have it live inside a week, it's mostly a switch in the directory. Caio at the helpdesk guessed fifteen tickets a week or so while people get used to it.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Fifteen a week is fine. What's the gateway charge per message, though?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Uh, I don't have it in front of me. Maybe two cents? I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Two cents times, say, a couple of logins a day each... that's, hm, I'll work it out later.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's tiny whatever it is. Compared to buying 220 of those little key things.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sure, cheap. But a stolen phone number, someone just ports it over, and then what?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's, I mean, that does happen. Probably rare for a company our size?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Probably. I'm just saying write it down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Clara's thing was more about having anything at all than the strongest thing, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: That was my read, yes. She said, um, "evidence of a second step", something like that.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Did she give a date she'd re-check?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not that I remember. Oh, speaking of dates, did anyone book the room for the offsite? Anika asked me twice.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I thought Paolo was doing that.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: He said he was, then he said Camille had a contact. I honestly lost track.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Camille's contact had a venue with no windows. I saw the photos.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ha, no. Okay, I'll chase Paolo. Where was I?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Sign-in codes. Phones.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right. Sorry, I keep going sideways. My sister's moving flat this weekend and I'm roped in, so my brain's just - boxes.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Stairs?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fourth floor, no elevator. I know. Anyway.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Can I ask one more awkward thing about the phones?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: You will anyway.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: What about people on the factory floor who aren't allowed phones in the building?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Oh. Um. I think maybe that's a handful of people? I'm not sure how many exactly.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: It's the warehouse badge-in crowd. Around twelve, going by the last headcount sheet.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: They don't sign in on the floor though, they sign in at the front office, right?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Some do, some use the shared terminal. I'd have to ask.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Let's park that. It's a detail, not a blocker.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I wasn't saying blocker. Just, someone's going to ask on day one.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fair, and that'll be in the fifteen tickets.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Probably, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can I ask about the laptop refresh while we're all here? Is that still happening this year?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Different topic, but yes, finance said the second half. Not my favorite answer.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Second half is vague.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's what I've got. Sven, you had the quote?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Two quotes. The cheaper one is for 90 machines, the other covers 140 but the spec is older.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Older how?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Previous generation processor. Fine for email, rough for the design folks.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, I want to get the sign-in thing done first. Everybody okay with the phone codes idea so far?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'm fine with it. Big picture it gets us moving.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'm fine as long as the porting thing is noted.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Fine with me if the gateway price comes in near what Wei said.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I'll look it up right after, I can message everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's text-message codes for staff sign-in, that's what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Great. Um, do you want me to write the rollout note?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Yes please, short one, and cc Samir so he knows.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Should that go to all staff or just managers first?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Managers first, a day before. Otherwise my inbox explodes.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll add the warehouse question to my list.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: And I'll write up the number-porting thing, one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Perfect. Oh, and the printer renewal, I'll reply to Samir today.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Tell him no to three years.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'll be politer than that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Slightly.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Slightly, yes. Sven, send me the laptop quotes so I can forward them to finance.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: They're in the shared folder, named by vendor. I'll send the links anyway.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thanks. I've got another call in two minutes, so I have to go.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same, actually.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, I think that's everyone. Wei, you're here, I see you now.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, my camera was being weird. I think maybe it's fixed.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Good. So before anything, has anyone heard back about the offsite room? Paolo said he'd -

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: He sent a message at like nine last night. Something about a hall with a deposit.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: A deposit. Of course there's a deposit.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: How much of a deposit?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: He didn't say, he just said "deposit, will confirm."

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: That is not confirming. I'll ping him after this.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Can I jump in before we lose the thread on the sign-in stuff? I pulled some numbers over the week.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Please, yes. That's the actual agenda, I'm just rambling.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: So the rollout's been live, what, a bit over a week now. But I also went back through the helpdesk log for the whole last month, the carrier support requests.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Oh, um, the ones from Caio's queue?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Yes. Caio flagged them to me. In that month there were six cases where somebody rang a carrier pretending to be one of our people and asked to move the number onto a new SIM.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Six. Out of 220 staff.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Six tries, and one of them went through. One.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Went through meaning-

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Meaning the carrier actually did it. The attacker had the number for a while, and used it to get codes.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Wait, hang on. Who was it?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: One of the executives. I'd rather not say which in a call with this many people on it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fine, fine. What did they get into?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: The mailbox. It was open for, I wrote it down, forty minutes, before anyone noticed and killed the session.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Forty minutes is, um, that's quite a long time, I think.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Was anything actually taken?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Unclear. Logs show it was opened and searched, I don't know what was read.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. That's - yeah. That's a lot to take in on a Friday.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Hold on, this isn't a thing I can just nod at. The codes by text message are exactly what they grabbed.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: That's the whole route in. Whoever owns the number gets the code, and we're telling people that's their second step.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, but devil's advocate, one in six isn't a rate I'd panic over.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's one in the first month. We've barely started.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, I know, I'm only saying the denominator matters.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: We can't defend keeping it. If Clara reads this, what do we say?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Let me think about what Clara would actually say, because-

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: She'd say it's still better than a password alone.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sure, until it isn't.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I think maybe, um, there could be a way to make the carrier harder to fool? Like a PIN on the account?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Some carriers offer that. Not all of them, and we don't control our people's personal plans.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Right. No, that's true.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Are these personal phones or company ones?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Mixed. Mostly personal, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Then we really can't tell the carrier anything.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, so two things I'm hearing. One, the numbers. Two, Lena says we can't stand behind it.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Yes. Pretty much.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And Mateo, you're not disagreeing with the numbers?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Not the numbers. I'm just not sure what we replace it with, and by when.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: End of April, the audit date. That hasn't moved.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right, and that's five or six weeks.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Five and a bit. Which is tight if we also change the rollout midway.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Then we'd better start looking now rather than later.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Sure. Hm. Do we even know what the options cost?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Not yet. I haven't priced anything, I only looked at the incident side.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: The key things were expensive, if I remember. Wasn't it per person?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Per person, yes, but I don't have the figure. Don't quote me on any number there.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And an app on the phone, that'd be - what, free?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Depends who makes it. Some of them charge per seat.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I don't want to swing this around in the last ten minutes with half the facts.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It's not half the facts. We know what was captured.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I know. I hear you. But I also haven't read the log myself, and I'd like to, before anyone tells Clara or Samir anything.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I can send the log extract. It's four pages, maybe five.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Please. Today if you can.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: After lunch.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Do you want me to write down what's in the log for the notes?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Um, no, Sven's sending it, that's enough. Actually, yes, one line in the notes that we raised it.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay, I'll put it as an open item.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: What does staying put mean for this week? Do the managers keep getting their codes by text?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Yes, for now. Nothing changes until we've talked again.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I'd like that on record as me not being happy.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Noted, truly. It's noted.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, so I'm going to hold off on this, and we pick it up next week with the log in front of everyone. Maybe someone can bring a rough list of the other ways to do it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I can do a list. Just names, no pricing.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll try to get the pricing for at least two of them.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Great, thanks both. Oh, before we go, quickly, the laptop quotes. Did finance reply?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Not yet. I'll nudge them Monday.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thanks. I feel like every item today ends with someone replying later.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: That's most of this job.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ha, it is. My sister texted, by the way, she survived the move. Fourth floor, still no elevator.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Was she annoyed?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: She's sore. I carried one bookshelf and I'm sore too.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Aw. I think maybe a heating pad helps? That's what I use.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Good tip, thank you. Okay, I need to hop to another call, so I'll stop here.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same, I'm already late.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll send the extract right after.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thanks everybody.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Bye, um, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, is that everyone? Wei, I see you, Lena's on, Mateo, Sven. Good, we're all here.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Morning. Or afternoon, depending where you are.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ha. Friday afternoon for me and I already want the weekend. Before we start, did Paolo ever confirm that deposit for the offsite hall?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: He did. Three hundred, refundable if we cancel two weeks out.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Refundable is fine. Fine. I'll tell Anika it's sorted.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Is the hall the one with the windows?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: It has windows. Big ones. Camille checked.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Wonderful. Okay, now the other thing, which I've been thinking about all week.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I read the log extract on Tuesday, all five pages, and then I read it again. After that I honestly can't sit on the text codes any longer, so I want to take the sign-in question back up properly today. Anyone object to that?

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: No. I've been waiting for you to say it.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I think maybe that's, um, the right call? Given what was in the log.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I've got nothing against it. I did bring a couple of numbers though.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Good, hold those for a second. Mateo, you said you'd bring a list of the other ways to do this.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I did. Four names, one line each. An app on the phone, a push approval thing, the little physical keys, and a fingerprint-on-laptop option.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And you cut it down since then, didn't you? I saw something in the shared folder.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, I wrote a short note. It ended up mostly about one of them.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: The physical one, right? I read it last night.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. Lena, you read it, so walk us through it. Mateo can correct you.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sure, sure. So, big picture, his argument is that the number thing just stops mattering. Nobody can port a key, it's in your pocket or it isn't.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And the fake sign-in pages, the ones that ask for your code and pass it along, those don't work against it either. It checks which site you're actually on. That's the phishing bit.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: That's accurate. Keep going, you're doing fine.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Um, cost. He had it at about twenty-eight a head. So for all of us, 220 people, it comes to, what was it, 6,160. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: 6,160, yeah. I got the quote from the supplier on Wednesday, it's good until the end of next month.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And there was a test run. Fifteen people had them for, I don't remember, a few weeks? And nobody opened a ticket. Not one.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Three weeks. Fifteen people, zero tickets. I checked Caio's queue to be sure.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Zero is a nice number to see after what we saw last week.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Was the pilot, um, was it people who like this stuff? I think maybe that skews it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Fair question. It was mixed. Two from finance, three from the warehouse office, the rest were us and the helpdesk.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay. That's, yeah, that's more mixed than I assumed.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Can I put the text message numbers next to that? For the cost side?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Gateway was coming out around two cents a message, like Wei guessed. Over a year that's a few hundred, not a lot. So the codes are cheaper, no question.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Cheaper but we had one get through in the first month.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'm not arguing. Just saying the difference is about six thousand, give or take.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: And six thousand is less than one executive mailbox incident would cost us, if somebody ever looked at it that way.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I wouldn't put a figure on that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, me neither.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, devil's advocate time, and Mateo, I know it's usually you, but I'll do it. What about the people who lose them?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Lose the keys? Yeah, that happens. You order a few spares. The quote has twenty extra in it, I think. Or ten. I'd have to look.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Twenty. Page two.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Page two, there you go.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And if someone's on holiday and loses it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Then they call the helpdesk and we send a spare. It's not elegant. Neither is waiting for a carrier to answer.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: What about the warehouse people? The ones without phones on the floor?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: That was the twelve. A key doesn't need a phone, so that actually clears that one.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Oh. Right. I think maybe I forgot that part of the list.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: It was in the note, bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I keep getting distracted. Sorry. My sister called me at lunch, she's finally unpacked and wants to host everyone, and I said yes without thinking about who'd be doing the cooking.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Fourth floor, still?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fourth floor, still. We are all going to be carrying wine up the stairs.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Bring a spare key, in case she forgets hers.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Ha. No. Okay. Stop. Back.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: How long to switch everyone over, if it came to that? We have the end of April.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Delivery's about ten days. Then it's handing them out. I'd say small group sessions, twenty people at a time, so we're not doing 220 one by one.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Eleven or twelve sessions then.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Roughly. Could be ten if people come in bigger groups.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Do they all need to be in person?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Better if so. Ten minutes each, you register it, you test it, you leave.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Could I help with a session? I think maybe I'd be okay at that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes please. I'd like two people per session anyway.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And the old text codes stay on during all that?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: They'd have to. Until the last session at least.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, that makes sense. So nobody locked out halfway through.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And managers first again, I'd say. Like last time.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Sure. One day ahead, same as before.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Mailbox note goes to Samir as well, I'd guess.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Cc Samir, yes, he likes to know. And Clara needs a line before the end of next week, I'm not going to make her find out from the audit tracker.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I can write that one. Short.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep it dry. No adjectives.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I don't do adjectives.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: You do, a few. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Mateo, I'm happy with all of this. Can you place the order today, and get the group sessions on everybody's calendar before the end of next week? Wei will help you run them.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yep, I'll send the purchase request after this and book the first slots for the week after next.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Do you want me to forward the quote to finance, or will you?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll do it. I have the PDF open.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Okay. Their sign-off is usually a day or two.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Tell them it's tied to the audit date, that tends to speed them up.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I can start on the instructions for the sessions. I think maybe a one-page thing?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: One page. With pictures if you can.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: Okay, I'll try.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Should I mention the spares in the note to Clara?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Just the count, no detail. She'll ask if she wants more.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: The laptop quotes, by the way. Finance finally replied. They want it as one line in next quarter's request.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Of course they do. Fine, I'll write it up Monday.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll send you the vendor names again.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Please. Okay, I've got a call at the top of the hour, so I have to run.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Same here, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone. Good week, actually, despite everything.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Bye.
